name: MKI Media Hero
overview: A cinematic hero banner on the Jellyfin home screen.
description: Adds a full-width hero carousel to the Jellyfin home screen. The list is prepared on the server from recently added, top rated and (optionally) Seerr trending titles, filtered per library with title, genre, tag and rating whitelists and blacklists. Layout, transitions, text and buttons are configurable.

versions.changelog: Security update. Every user now gets their own banner that follows their library access, parental controls and blocked tags, instead of one list for everyone, and banners are never shared between accounts in the browser cache. Calls to Seerr no longer follow redirects or keep cookies, and library names on the settings page are escaped.
The API key on the settings page is hidden by default; the eye button shows it.

Cleans up an older copy of this plugin left behind by an update or rename: the old copy is marked for removal and stays inactive, so it can no longer break requests. Restart Jellyfin once to finish the cleanup. Settings are kept.
English only: settings page, labels and log messages are now in English. Redesigned, cleaner settings page with tabs and status indicators. Settings are kept.
Renamed to MKI Media Hero so all MKI plugins sit together in the plugin list. Settings are kept.
Jellyseerr is now Seerr: renamed the trending sources and all labels. Settings are kept.
Per-library targets, sources as upper limits, paged Jellyseerr trending lookup, browser caching and a background pre-warmer.

name: MKI Merge Versions
overview: Two resolutions, one entry. The 4K version leads.
description: Merges movies that exist in several resolutions into a single library entry, matched by TMDb ID (IMDb as fallback), never by title. The highest resolution becomes the primary version. Runs as a scheduled task and automatically once the library has been quiet for five minutes. Includes a dry-run mode.

versions.changelog: Security update. Versions are only linked when exactly the same users can see them and they share a production year, so merging can no longer reveal a file from a library someone has no access to. Existing links that break this are split again, stale links are released, groups of more than eight versions are skipped, and two runs can no longer overlap.

Cleans up an older copy of this plugin left behind by an update or rename: the old copy is marked for removal and stays inactive, so it can no longer break requests. Restart Jellyfin once to finish the cleanup. Settings are kept.
English only: settings page, labels and log messages are now in English. Redesigned, cleaner settings page with tabs and status indicators. Settings are kept.
First release: links versions via the database, groups by TMDb/IMDb, highest resolution becomes primary, own settings page.

name: MKI Password Policy
overview: Password rules and forced password changes for Jellyfin users.
description: Enforces password rules (length, character types, no username, common passwords) on the server for every client, with ready-made profiles. Lets an administrator require a new password from all users or from single users, right away or with a notice period: they cannot sign in on any device until they have set one. Accounts without a password are locked until they get a temporary password. Web-based apps show a popup users must answer; TVs get Jellyfin's message window and a change page that opens in any browser.

versions.changelog: Security update. A blocked user's token is now refused however it is sent (any authorization header, the older header names or the query string), and a request carrying tokens of several users is refused. When a deadline passes, the user's tokens are revoked within a minute, a sign-in that gets through on any path is undone at once, and setting a new password signs out every other device.

Accounts without a password that have a profile or a request are now locked right away on every sign-in path (apps, TVs, Quick Connect, existing sessions), with no notice period, and nobody can claim them by name: new Temporary password button shows a random password once and the user replaces it at the next sign-in. Passwords an administrator sets (Jellyfin's Password tab or new users) and reset PINs now count as temporary for users with a profile. A second request can only bring a deadline forward. Bulk requests never include the admin who sends them. Web-based apps show a popup that must be answered during a notice period; TVs get Jellyfin's message window instead of a fading toast. Settings page: every change applies immediately, no Save button, with a question before anything locks accounts.

New notice period when requiring a new password (right away, or 1, 3, 7 or 14 days): users keep access until the deadline and every app they use, TVs included, shows a message with the deadline and the change link, at most once a day per device. The list shows the deadline and which devices were reminded. New Copy message for users button with a ready text to send.

Disabled users can get profiles and password requests, also from the buttons for many users; they apply once the account is enabled again. With exempt administrators on, administrators are greyed out in the list. Each user's Password tab in the dashboard now shows their profile, password status and any request, with a shortcut to them in the plugin settings. Live hints on that tab now use the rules of the user being edited.

The change dialog now stays above everything, including the Jellyfin loading spinner, and lists the password rules for your account. A profile picked for a user in the list is saved immediately, so requiring a new password right after picking it no longer drops the choice.
All text is now in English.
First release.

name: MKI Seerr Bridge
overview: Seerr inside Jellyfin: button, embedded view, search and sign-in.
description: Brings Seerr into the Jellyfin web client: a button in the header and side menu, Seerr embedded in Jellyfin instead of a redirect, Seerr suggestions under Jellyfin search results with one-click requests attributed to the right user, optional single sign-on via Quick Connect, and a compatibility bridge for clients that still send legacy X-Emby authorization headers.

versions.changelog: Security update. Requests from the search results are made in the user's own Seerr account, matched by Jellyfin user ID, and are refused for accounts not linked to Seerr yet instead of running as the administrator; each user can send up to 30 per hour. Single sign-on can no longer be triggered by other websites, and the Seerr session cookie is set HttpOnly (and Secure over https). The settings endpoint needs a signed-in user, the plugin repository answers only inside the local network, the legacy header bridge only passes a single well-formed token, and calls to Seerr no longer follow redirects or keep cookies.
The API key on the settings page is hidden by default; the eye button shows it.

Cleans up an older copy of this plugin left behind by an update or rename: the old copy is marked for removal and stays inactive, so it can no longer break requests. Restart Jellyfin once to finish the cleanup. Settings are kept. Single sign-on now steps aside on any error instead of blocking sign-in.
English only: settings page, labels and log messages are now in English. Redesigned, cleaner settings page with tabs and status indicators. Settings are kept.
Renamed to MKI Seerr Bridge so all MKI plugins sit together in the plugin list. Settings are kept.
Renamed to Seerr Bridge: Jellyseerr is now Seerr. All labels, descriptions and the menu route (#/seerr) follow the new name. Settings are kept.
Header and side-menu button, embedded view, search suggestions with requests, single sign-on via Quick Connect, legacy auth header bridge.
